issues.detail: The Greek 'εκτεινειν' (ekteinein) literally means 'to stretch out' or 'to extend'. The Vietnamese translation 'để chữa lành' (to heal) is a functional/interpretive addition. While the context implies healing, the Greek text itself only says 'stretching out your hand'.

The phrase 'σε εις ιασιν' (se eis iasin) meaning 'upon you [for] healing' is partially lost or transformed into the adverbial purpose 'để chữa lành'. The Greek specifies that the stretching out of the hand is directed *toward* healing.
